column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“From affliction” is rendered “under affliction,” and “abundance of servitude” as “harsh servitude.”
“Afflicted” follows the Hebrew; the LXX reads “led away.”
“Become a head” is rendered “become her masters,” and “at ease” as “prosper.”
The written text has an extra letter (“from”) that is not read; “deer” is rendered “bucks.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Sin she has sinned” is rendered “sinned greatly,” and “impurity” as “an unclean thing.”
“Remembered” is rendered “consider,” and “wonders” as “astonishingly.”
Close to the Hebrew.

Close to the Hebrew.
“Mastered it” is rendered “prevailed over them.”
“Bound on” follows an uncertain verb; the meaning is uncertain.
“Thrown away” is rendered “rejected,” and NASB supplies “as in.”
“My eye, my eye” is rendered “My eyes”; NASB drops the repetition.
“Commanded of Jacob” is rendered “commanded concerning Jacob.”
“His mouth” is rendered “His command.”
“Restore their life” is rendered “restore their strength.”
“My inward parts are in turmoil” is rendered “My spirit is greatly troubled.”
“You have brought” is rendered as a wish, “Oh, that You would bring.”
Close to the Hebrew.
